claims.text: Urine preg test in every woman of childbearing age; a (−) result effectively rules out ruptured ectopic preg.
claims.quote: A bedside urine pregnancy test should be done for all women of childbearing age because a negative result effectively excludes ruptured ectopic pregnancy.

claims.text: Serum lipase: strongly suggests acute pancreatitis.
claims.quote: An exception is serum lipase, which strongly suggests a diagnosis of acute pancreatitis.

claims.text: CBC, chemistries and UA are often sent but are nonspecific; serious dz can have norm results.
claims.quote: Standard tests (eg, complete blood count, chemistries, urinalysis) are often done but are of little value due to poor specificity; patients with significant disease may have normal results.

claims.text: Abd series (flat and upright abd plus upright chest film) when perf or obstruct = sus.
claims.quote: An abdominal series, consisting of flat and upright abdominal radiographs and upright chest radiographs (left lateral recumbent abdomen and anteroposterior chest radiograph for patients unable to stand), should be done when perforation or obstruction is suspected.

claims.text: US for sus biliary dz, ectopic preg (transvaginal) or appendicitis in children.
claims.quote: Ultrasound should be done for suspected biliary tract disease or ectopic pregnancy (transvaginal probe) and for suspected appendicitis in children.

claims.text: Noncontrast helical CT for sus renal stones.
claims.quote: Noncontrast helical CT is the modality of choice for suspected renal stones

claims.text: CT w oral and IV contrast = diagnostic in about ≥ 95% of pts w sig abd pain, but imaging must ⍉delay surg when the signs are definitive.
claims.quote: CT with oral and IV contrast is diagnostic in approximately ≥ 95% of patients with significant abdominal pain and has markedly lowered the negative laparotomy rate. However, advanced imaging must not be allowed to delay surgery in patients with definitive symptoms and signs.
